_comment: L2.c of docs/2026-09-07_latent_intent_design.zh.md: the beta CALIBRATION after L2_gauss collapsed at beta=1.0 (active_units 0.0 from epoch ~8, KL 0.0016 nats/flight; L2_mix4 predicted to do the same). The units argument: the reconstruction term is a scaled MSE — position in (m / position_loss_scale_m=10 km)^2 — so the whole 962 m of hidden intent is worth (0.096)^2 = 0.009 loss units, while a 4-way decision costs log 4 = 1.4 nats; at beta=1 the KL is ~150x the entire gain z could buy, and collapse is the optimum, not a pathology. beta must be of the order of the loss units per nat: a decade ladder 0.1 / 0.01 / 0.001 on the SAME base as l2_latent_arms.json (K=1, analytic KL, free bits 0.05/dim kept for comparability; annealing not added — a too-high final beta collapses after any warm-up). Arms differ only in latent_beta. READOUT as l2_latent_arms.json (predict_args write modes/, random/, shuffled/). PRE-REGISTERED READING: per arm, active_units at the best epoch, kl_nats_per_flight, shuffled delta-ADE, minADE_6 vs top-1 vs the same-K N(0,I) control, top-1 vs L1_native32 per stratum; the calibration picks the LARGEST beta that passes gate (1) (active_units >= 3 AND shuffled delta-ADE > 200 m) and whose top-1 is not worse than L1_native32 beyond seed noise; that beta then goes to K=4 and to the z-oracle arms (l2_zoracle_arms.json). VETO as before: straight-in top-1 FDE degraded beyond seed noise. If NO beta passes gate (1) without costing the top-1, the decoder is explaining the data without z (the imitation teacher pins the controls to the inverse-dynamics target) and the next lever is the posterior's input, not beta.
